items.title: Carnegie Mellon is putting computer science courses on YouTube for free
items.summary: Carnegie Mellon University has launched a new initiative to offer free computer science courses on YouTube, making high-quality education accessible to a global audience. This move is significant for developers and engineers looking to enhance their skills without financial barriers.

items.title: Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use
items.summary: Recent findings reveal that Windows 11 is tracking user data related to coding agents and developer tools, raising privacy concerns among developers. This information is crucial for engineers to understand how their data is being utilized and to take necessary precautions.

items.title: Technical issue at JPMorgan Chase triggers online banking delays for US banks
items.summary: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase has caused widespread online banking delays affecting multiple US banks, highlighting the vulnerabilities in banking systems architecture. This incident serves as a reminder for engineers to prioritize system reliability and contingency planning.

items.title: Optimizely Compromised, Served Malware on Zoom, GitLab
items.summary: Optimizely has been compromised, leading to malware being served on platforms like Zoom and GitLab, affecting numerous users. Developers must be vigilant about security practices and the integrity of third-party tools they integrate into their workflows.

items.title: Jiff 1.0: A datetime library for Rust
items.summary: The release of Jiff 1.0, a new datetime library for Rust, offers developers enhanced functionality for handling date and time operations. This library is a valuable addition to the Rust ecosystem, promoting better coding practices and efficiency.
